Listed at {{height|ft=6|in=11}} and {{Convert|250|lb}},{{cite web|title=Goga Bitadze|url=https://www.nba.com/player/1629048/goga-bitadze/bio|website=NBA.com|access-date=7 August 2025|archive-date=27 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210527062151/https://www.nba.com/player/1629048/goga-bitadze/bio|url-status=live}} he plays the [[center (basketball)|center]] position. He was drafted 18th overall by the [[Indiana Pacers]] in the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web |last=Kalbrosky |first=Bryan |date=22 January 2019 |title=2019 aggregate NBA mock draft 4.0: Murray State's Ja Morant is Top 3 |url=https://www.hoopshype.com/story/sports/nba/draft/2019/01/22/nba-mock-draft-big-board-rumor-update-prospects/82921993007/ |access-date=6 February 2019 |website=HoopsHype.com}}{{cite magazine|first=Jeremy|last=Woo|title=2019 NBA Mock Draft 3.0: Zion Williamson Remains on Top, Ja Morant Continues to Skyrocket|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2019/01/30/nba-mock-draft-2019-zion-williamson-rj-barrett-ja-morant-cam-reddish|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=30 January 2019|access-date=6 February 2019|archive-date=7 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207015825/https://www.si.com/nba/2019/01/30/nba-mock-draft-2019-zion-williamson-rj-barrett-ja-morant-cam-reddish|url-status=live}} Born in [[Sagarejo]], Bitadze started playing basketball professionally with [[B.C. VITA Tbilisi|VITA Tbilisi]] in the [[VTB United League]]. In 2015, he moved to Serbian club Mega Basket and was loaned to [[Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]] team [[KK Smederevo 1953|Smederevo 1953]] in the following year. Upon his return to Mega in 2017–18, Bitadze was named [[most valuable player]] (MVP) of the [[Junior ABA League]] and became a key player for the senior team. At the end of 2018, he was loaned to [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost]] in [[Montenegro]] and was named [[EuroLeague Rising Star]] for the 2018–19 season. Bitadze is a member of the [[Georgia men's national basketball team|Georgian national basketball team]]. He was named to the national team at [[EuroBasket 2017]] and made his debut at [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|FIBA World Cup qualifiers]] in 2017. Previously, Bitadze represented Georgia at the junior level in [[FIBA]] competition. ==Early life and career== Bitadze was born in [[Sagarejo]], a town in eastern [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]].{{cite web |last=Hein |first=David |title=Bitadze goes from land of wrestlers to talent-developing Mega |url=http://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/7rc5kkcryt8dtc4f/bitadze-goes-from-land-of-wrestlers-to-talent-developing-mega |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |access-date=30 January 2019 |date=21 April 2017 |archive-date=4 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190204222022/http://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/7rc5kkcryt8dtc4f/bitadze-goes-from-land-of-wrestlers-to-talent-developing-mega |url-status=live }} His father was a professional basketball player whose career was cut short by injury.{{cite web |last=Simonishvili |first=Vazha |title=NBA-ის კემპი, იოკიჩი, ფაჩულია - ინტერვიუ გოგა ბითაძესთან |url=https://sportall.ge/kalatburti/qarthuli-kalathburthi/legionerebi/105511-nba-is-kempi-iokichi-fachulia-interviu-goga-bithadzesthan.html |publisher=SportAll |access-date=30 January 2019 |language=ka |date=25 June 2017 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207020352/https://sportall.ge/kalatburti/qarthuli-kalathburthi/legionerebi/105511-nba-is-kempi-iokichi-fachulia-interviu-goga-bithadzesthan.html |url-status=live }} Although Bitadze did not watch basketball in his childhood, he started playing the game when he was six years old, because he saw himself as "active and tall." As he became more involved in basketball, he began idolizing Georgian players [[Zaza Pachulia]] and [[Tornike Shengelia]], as well as NBA stars [[Pau Gasol]] and [[Shaquille O'Neal]].{{cite AV media|people=Bitadze, Goga, and Jonathan Givony|date=12 September 2016|title=Goga Bitadze Interview from NBA Basketball Without Borders Europe Camp|medium=Video|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kZrf8aEjZfY|location=[[Finland]]|publisher=DraftExpress|access-date=6 February 2019|archive-date=19 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220519000845/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kZrf8aEjZfY|url-status=live}} On 31 May 2013, Bitadze scored 17 points to help his school team [[Hyundai Motor Company|Hyundai]] win the national under-14 championship over Gori.{{cite web |title=1-ელი ექსპერიმენტალური სკოლის გუნდი "ჰიუნდაი" ჩემპიონია! |url=http://gbf.ge/league/u14/news/1-eli-eqsperimentaluri-skolis-gundi-hiundai-chempionia |publisher=[[Georgian Basketball Federation]] |access-date=30 January 2019 |language=ka |date=31 May 2013}} He also played in the Georgian under-16 league for three years. In 2014–15, his final season with Hyundai at the under-16 level, Bitadze averaged 23.1 points, 16.6 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 3.8 blocks per game.{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze |url=http://gbf.ge/en/league/u16/player/5552711 |publisher=[[Georgian Basketball Federation]] |access-date=30 January 2019}} Through his early career, Bitadze trained in the junior ranks of Georgian club [[B.C. |url-status=live }} ==Professional career== ===VITA Tbilisi (2015–2016)=== In the 2015–16 season, Bitadze played professionally for VITA Tbilisi in the [[VTB United League]].{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Goga-Bitadze/Summary/75906 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=31 January 2019 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207020209/https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Goga-Bitadze/Summary/75906 |url-status=live }} He made his debut at age 16 and consequently became the youngest player in league history.{{cite web |last=Kharazov |first=Levan |title=გოგა ბითაძე სერბულ "მეგა ლეკსში" გადავიდა |url=https://www.mysports.ge/ka/post/view/2132 |publisher=MySports |url-status=dead }} Through six games, Bitadze averaged 2.8 points, 1.7 rebounds and 0.7 blocks in 13.8 minutes per game.{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze |url=http://old.vtb-league.com/en/player/goga-bitadze.htm |publisher=[[VTB United League]] |access-date=31 January 2019 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207015924/http://old.vtb-league.com/en/player/goga-bitadze.htm |url-status=dead }} ===Mega Basket (2015–2019)=== ====Junior success and Smederevo loan (2015–2017)==== On 2 December 2015, Bitadze signed with [[KK Mega Basket|Mega Basket]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia]] (KLS) and [[ABA League]].{{cite web |last=Obradovic |first=Igor |title=Goga Bitadze (ex Vita Tbilisi) joins Mega Leks |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Serbia/news/429985/Former-players:-Goga-Bitadze-(ex-Vita-Tbilisi)-joins-Mega-Leks |publisher=[[Eurobasket.com|Eurobasket]] |access-date=31 January 2019 |date=2 December 2015 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207020016/https://www.eurobasket.com/Serbia/news/429985/Former-players:-Goga-Bitadze-(ex-Vita-Tbilisi)-joins-Mega-Leks |url-status=live }} Bitadze was drawn to the club because it had produced many NBA players like [[Nikola Jokić]] and [[Ivica Zubac]], and he thought the Serbian league was "well run."{{cite web |last=Rangelov |first=Miloš |title=Ko je Goga Bitadze? Gruzijac od kojeg Mega pravi novog Jokića |url=https://sport.blic.rs/kosarka/domaca-kosarka-i-aba/cudo-od-deteta-ko-je-goga-bitadze-gruzijac-od-kojeg-mega-pravi-novog-jokica/j4h58te |website=[[Blic]] |access-date=1 February 2019 |language=sr |date=21 May 2017 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207015908/https://sport.blic.rs/kosarka/domaca-kosarka-i-aba/cudo-od-deteta-ko-je-goga-bitadze-gruzijac-od-kojeg-mega-pravi-novog-jokica/j4h58te |url-status=live }} He described the move, "It was hard for me for a couple of months. I was really frustrated, far away from my family and far away from my friends. It was hard, but then slowly I got used to it... you have to sacrifice in order to achieve something big and get something even bigger."{{cite web |last=Petrinovic |first=Igor |title=Goga Bitadze, Buducnost: 'We are not going to give up' |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/interviews/euroleague-2018-19/i/9ecubovhtrpe8eu6/goga-bitadze-buducnost-we-are-not-going-to-give-up |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |access-date=31 January 2019 |date=15 January 2019 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207015838/http://www.euroleague.net/news/interviews/euroleague-2018-19/i/9ecubovhtrpe8eu6/goga-bitadze-buducnost-we-are-not-going-to-give-up |url-status=live }} In December 2015, Bitadze averaged 7.8 points and 4 rebounds per game to help Mega's junior team win the [[2015–16 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|Torneo Città di Roma]] and qualify for the [[2015–16 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|2015–16 Adidas Next Generation Tournament]] (ANGT).{{cite web |title=Final, Stellazzurra Basketball vs. Mega Leks Belgrade - Torneo Citta di Roma |url=http://admin.euroleague.net/u18/photos/2015-16/i/6ks6smaegigrphc4/final-stellazzurra-basketball-vs-mega-leks-belgrade-torneo-citta-di-roma |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |access-date=31 January 2019 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207072235/http://admin.euroleague.net/u18/photos/2015-16/i/6ks6smaegigrphc4/final-stellazzurra-basketball-vs-mega-leks-belgrade-torneo-citta-di-roma |url-status=live }} In three games at the ANGT, he averaged 4.7 points and 5.3 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Bitadze, Goga |url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=006809&seasoncode=JTR15 |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |access-date=31 January 2019 |archive-date=29 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161129145831/http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=006809&seasoncode=JTR15 |url-status=live }} For the 2016–17 season, Bitadze was [[Loan (sports)|loaned]] to Serbian club [[KK Smederevo 1953|Smederevo 1953]], which competed in the KLS.{{cite web |last=Givony |first=Jonathan |last2=Kamalsky |first2=Matt |title=2017 Adidas EuroCamp Rosters and Preview |url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/2017-adidas-eurocamp-rosters-and-preview-5987/ |publisher=DraftExpress |access-date=31 January 2019 |date=7 June 2017 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207015905/http://www.draftexpress.com/article/2017-adidas-eurocamp-rosters-and-preview-5987/ |url-status=dead }} Through 19 games, he averaged 10.6 points, 4.4 rebounds and 1.2 blocks per game. Bitadze debuted on 8 October 2016, recording 5 points and 4 rebounds in a 75–71 loss to [[KK Borac Čačak|Borac Čačak]].{{cite web |title=KK Smederevo 1953 71, KK Borac Cacak 75 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2016-10-08/KK-Smederevo-1953-at-KK-Borac-Cacak/253992 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=31 January 2019 |date=8 October 2016 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207020507/https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2016-10-08/KK-Smederevo-1953-at-KK-Borac-Cacak/253992 |url-status=live }} On 29 October versus [[KK Napredak Kruševac|Napredak Kruševac]], he scored a season-high 18 points, a mark he would match three more times in the season.{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze Game Logs |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Goga-Bitadze/GameLogs/75906/International/2017/13 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=31 January 2019 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207020600/https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Goga-Bitadze/GameLogs/75906/International/2017/13 |url-status=live }} Bitadze recorded his first [[double (basketball)|double-double]] on 1 April 2017 against [[OKK Dunav|Dunav Stari Banovci]], with 18 points and 11 rebounds.{{cite web |title=KK Smederevo 1953 86, KK Dunav Stari Banovci 75 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2017-04-01/KK-Smederevo-1953-at-KK-Dunav-Stari-Banovci/262976 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=31 January 2019 |date=1 April 2017 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207020505/https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2017-04-01/KK-Smederevo-1953-at-KK-Dunav-Stari-Banovci/262976 |url-status=live }} In addition, he assumed a leading role for the Mega Basket junior team at the [[2016–17 Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament|2016–17 ANGT]]. Bitadze averaged 17.7 points per game and led the tournament with 10 rebounds and 3.8 blocks per contest, en route to making the All-Tournament Team.{{cite web |title=ANGT MVP Fevrier of Paris headlines All-Tournament Team |url=http://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/7tq4fg39g34kcdfy/angt-mvp-fevrier-of-paris-headlines-all-tournament-team |publisher=[[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] |access-date=31 January 2019 |date=21 May 2017}} ====Rise to stardom (2017–2018)==== He returned to Mega entering the 2017–18 season and mainly played with the senior team. Through 22 games in the ABA League, Bitadze averaged 11.8 points, 6.2 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per game, and through 12 games in the KLS, he averaged 15.9 points and 6.7 rebounds per game.{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze Basketball Player Profile |url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Goga_Bitadze/KK_Buducnost_Voli_Podgorica/369053 |publisher=[[Eurobasket.com|Eurobasket]] |access-date=1 February 2019 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207015630/https://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Goga_Bitadze/KK_Buducnost_Voli_Podgorica/369053 |url-status=live }} He debuted on 1 October 2017, recording 12 points, 9 rebounds and 5 blocks in a 95–88 win over [[KK Cibona|Cibona]].{{cite web |title=KK Cibona 88, KK Mega Bemax 95 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2017-10-01/KK-Cibona-at-KK-Mega-Bemax/270477 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=1 February 2019 |date=1 October 2017 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207020411/https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2017-10-01/KK-Cibona-at-KK-Mega-Bemax/270477 |url-status=live }} In January 2018, Bitadze briefly played for Mega's junior team and helped capture the [[Junior ABA League]] championship. After averaging 17 points and 11 rebounds in the final tournament, he was named league MVP and earned Ideal Five recognition.{{cite web |title=The MVP award belongs to Goga Bitadze |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=39766 |publisher=[[ABA League]] |access-date=1 February 2019 |date=28 January 2018 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207020250/https://www.aba-liga.com/news.php?id=39766 |url-status=live }} On 20 January, Bitadze scored 23 points versus [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita]], his season-high mark in the ABA League.{{cite web |title=KK Mega Bemax 73, Cedevita 75 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2018-01-20/KK-Mega-Bemax-at-Cedevita/290471 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=3 February 2019 |date=20 January 2018 |archive-date=7 February 2019 games for Mega, all of which were in the ABA League, he averaged 20.2 points, 7.9 rebounds, and 2.6 blocks per game. ====Budućnost loan (2018–2019)==== On 20 December 2018, Bitadze was loaned to Montenegrin club [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost]], which at the time competed in top-tier continental [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web |title=Buducnost adds young star Bitadze |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9ca7iicfwhxyspfa/buducnost-adds-young-star-bitadze |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |access-date=4 February 2019 |date=20 December 2018 |archive-date=20 December 2018 the season.{{cite web |title=Bitadze on loan in Buducnost until the end of ABA League |url=http://www.bcmegabasket.net/en/2018/12/20/bitadze-na-pozajmici-u-buducnosti-do-kraja-aba-lige/ to his new club, Bitadze said, "It was not an easy situation, especially the first couple of days. I mean, it is still hard now to get used to things. But my teammates and coaches helped me." In his first game for Budućnost, on 24 December, he recorded 12 points and 4 rebounds versus [[KK Krka|Krka]] in the ABA League.{{cite web |title=Buducnost 64, Krka Novo Mesto 69 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2018-12-24/Buducnost-at-Krka-Novo-Mesto/322567 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=5 February 2019 |date=24 December 2018 |archive-date=7 later, Bitadze made his EuroLeague debut, chipping in 17 points, 7 rebounds and 4 blocks in a 93–88 loss to [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]].{{cite web |title=Bayern rallies from 17 down, overcomes Buducnost |url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=119&seasoncode=E2018#!report |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |access-date=5 February 2019 |date=28 December 2018 January 2019, he had another strong EuroLeague performance, posting 23 points, 8 rebounds and 3 blocks off the bench in a 111–94 defeat to [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Olimpia Milano]].{{cite web |title=Milan blasts Buducnost with record scoring performance |url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=122&seasoncode=E2018#!report |publisher=[[EuroLeague]] |access-date=5 averaged 12.1 points, 6.4 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game and claimed [[EuroLeague Rising Star]] honors as the best under-22 player in the EuroLeague.{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze named EuroLeague Rising Star |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/873787/goga-bitadze-named-euroleague-rising-star/ |publisher=EuroHoops |access-date=16 May 2019 |date=7 May 2019 |archive-date=16 May 2019 Pacers (2019–2023)=== [[File:Goga Bitadze (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Bitadze with the [[Indiana Pacers]] in 2022]] On 20 April 2019, Bitadze declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]], for which he was considered a possible [[NBA draft lottery|lottery]] pick.{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze officially declares for the NBA Draft |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/nba-news/865485/goga-bitadze-officially-declares-for-the-nba-draft/ |publisher=EuroHoops |access-date=20 June 2019 |date=20 April 2019 |archive-date=20 June 2019 availability for the draft, Bitadze appeared in a [[viral video|viral]] photo that showed him being ignored by reporters, who instead surrounded [[Zion Williamson]], the eventual [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]], in the background. A number of NBA players, including [[Dwyane Wade]] and [[Draymond Green]], suggested he use the photo as motivation.{{cite news |last=Boren |first=Cindy |title=Goga Bitadze is everyone's favorite NBA draft pick after his sad photo with Zion Williamson |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2019/06/20/goga-bitadze-is-everyones-favorite-nba-draft-pick-after-his-sad-photo-with-zion-williamson |url-status=live }}{{cite web |last=Weinrib |first=Ben |title=NBA stars reach out to draft prospect who gets ignored for Zion Williamson Pacers]] with the 18th pick overall in the [[2019 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Wheat|last=Hotchkiss|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/2019-draft-night-recap|title=Pacers Draft Goga Bitadze with 18th web|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-goga-bitadze|title=Pacers Sign Goga Bitadze|date=15 July 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=15 July 2019}} On 28 October 2019, Bitadze made his NBA debut, coming off the bench in a 110–99 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] with two points and a rebound.{{cite web |date=25 October 2019 |title=Cavaliers 110–99 Pacers box score – 25 October 2019 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401160672 |access-date=11 January 2025 |website=ESPN.com}} On 9 February 2023, Bitadze was waived by the Pacers after three-and-a-half seasons.{{Cite national team=== Bitadze played for the [[Georgia men's national under-16 basketball team|Georgian national under-17 team]] at the 2015 [[FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] Division B, averaging 14.2 points, 8.8 rebounds and 3.7 blocks per game en route to a fifth-place finish. He had his best scoring display in the tournament on 13 August 2015, posting 24 points and 11 rebounds in an 80–66 loss to Sweden.{{cite web |title=Georgia 66, Sweden 80 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/national/boxscore/2015-08-13/Georgia-at-Sweden/217916 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=6 February 2019 |date=13 August 2015 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207020639/https://basketball.realgm.com/national/boxscore/2015-08-13/Georgia-at-Sweden/217916 |url-status=live }} At the [[2016 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship Division B]], Bitadze averaged 11.4 points, 10.2 rebounds and 4.1 blocks per game for the [[Georgia national under-19 basketball team|Georgian under-18 team]].{{cite web |title=Goga Bitadze's profile |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/116061/pid2//sid/12385/tid/2187/tid2//_/2016_FIBA_U18_European_Championship_Division_B/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190223092631/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/116061/pid2/sid/12385/tid/2187/tid2/_/2016_FIBA_U18_European_Championship_Division_B/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=23 February 2019 |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=5 February 2019}} On 6 August 2016, he recorded tournament-best marks of 23 points and 9 blocks while grabbing 13 rebounds in a 103–101 win over Bulgaria.{{cite web |title=Georgia 103, Bulgaria 101 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/national/boxscore/2016-08-06/Georgia-at-Bulgaria/239336 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=6 February 2019 |date=6 August 2016 |archive-date=7 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190207020519/https://basketball.realgm.com/national/boxscore/2016-08-06/Georgia-at-Bulgaria/239336 |url-status=live }} Bitadze returned to national team play in 2017, averaging 10.9 points and 6.3 rebounds per game at the [[FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] Division B. ===Senior national team=== Bitadze was first named to the [[Georgia men's national basketball team|Georgian senior national team]] at [[EuroBasket 2017]], but a calf ligament injury forced him to sit out of the entire competition. Regardless, he "learned a lot on and off the court" by observing his veteran teammates, including [[Zaza Pachulia]] and [[Giorgi Shermadini]].{{cite web |title=Facing Raduljica, Zirbes helps Bitadze become big future hope for Georgia |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2019/european-qualifiers/news/facing-raduljica-zirbes-helps-bitadze-become-big-future-hope-for-georgia |publisher=[[FIBA]] |access-date=6 February 2019 |date=12 January 2018}} On 24 November 2017, Bitadze debuted for the senior national team versus [[Germany men's national basketball team|Germany]] during [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Europe)|qualification]] for the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA World Cup]], scoring 4 points in 17 minutes.{{cite web |title=Georgia 70, Germany 79 |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/national/boxscore/2017-11-24/Georgia-at-Germany/288805 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |access-date=6 February 2019 |date=24 November 2017 |archive-date=7
